packageRules.description: Same policy as the homelab repository: patch and minor automerge, majors wait for a human. No groups -- every workload gets its own PR.

A PostgreSQL major version is an offline migration that takes the workload down while it runs, and it is not reversible. It waits for a human even though the image tag makes it look like any other bump. See cloudnative-pg.md in the homelab docs.

Home Assistant versions its releases as calendar dates, which semver reads as a major bump every month. Without this every routine release would wait for a human and none of them would ever be automerged.

customManagers.description: CloudNativePG names its operand image in `imageName`, which holds a complete image reference rather than a bare tag, so neither the kubernetes manager nor a tag-shaped comment manager reads it. `currentDigest` is what lets `config:best-practices` pin the digest; without that group the pin has nowhere to go and the whole pin branch errors.
Track versions annotated with a `# renovate:` comment. Needed for image tags written inline in a Helm `valuesObject:`, which the helm-values manager only reads from real values files.
